title: Before DNA and Protein: The RNA World Hypothesis vs. Metabolism-First Vents & RNA-Peptide Coevolution — Breaking the DNA-to-protein chicken-and-egg deadlock; Gilbert's 1986 RNA World & Ban, Nissen, Moore & Steitz's 2.4-angstrom proof that no protein touches the ribosome's peptidyl-transferase center within 18 angstroms; Powner, Gerland & Sutherland's 2-aminooxazole bypass, Becker & Carell's wet-dry purine-pyrimidine synthesis & Stairs, Szostak & Powner's divergent 8-oxopurine chemistry; Martin & Russell's hydrothermal FeS/NiS metabolism-first rival, Bernhardt's hydrolysis/chirality audit & Carter & Wills's aaRS urzyme RNP World; Eigen error-threshold & duplex-melting hydrolysis math plus spotting RNA-origin tests in disguise

teenKit.tldr: Life faces a brutal chicken-and-egg problem: DNA needs proteins to replicate, but proteins need DNA blueprints to form. The RNA World hypothesis solves this by showing how ancient RNA molecules could do both jobs at once—storing genetic information and acting as chemical catalysts.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how molecular machinery first sparked to life gives us the ultimate playbook for engineering synthetic biology, curing stubborn diseases, and searching for alien life across the universe.
keyTakeaways: The Central Dogma loop creates a deadlock because DNA requires proteins to copy itself, and proteins require DNA codes to build.

Ribosomes—the protein factories in every living cell—are living proof of an RNA-dominated past, because high-resolution crystal structures show that only RNA touches the active site where peptide bonds are forged.

Prebiotic chemistry experiments by scientists like Sutherland and Carell show that raw chemical building blocks can form nucleic acid pieces under early Earth conditions, bypassing the impossible need for fully formed modern biology to appear overnight.

quiz.question: What makes naked double-stranded DNA utterly useless on its own for starting life from scratch?
options: It breaks apart too easily in water.
It is catalytically dead and cannot copy itself without proteins.
It can only exist inside modern bacterial membranes.
quiz.explanation: While DNA is an amazing hard drive for data storage, it cannot perform any chemical reactions or copy itself without the help of protein enzymes.

quiz.question: What did Nenad Ban and his colleagues discover about the ribosome's peptide-bond-forming center at 2.4-angstrom resolution?
options: It is packed tightly with structural proteins.
It is made entirely of lipids.
Zero protein atoms are within 18 angstroms of the active site.
quiz.explanation: The atomic structure proved that only RNA touches the catalytic center, showing that the ribosome is fundamentally an ancient ribozyme.

quiz.question: What is the core argument of the metabolism-first hydrothermal vent hypothesis?
options: Life began when random DNA fell from comets into deep oceans.
Energy-driven chemical reactions powered by mineral surfaces came before genetic blueprints.
Proteins evolved millions of years before amino acids were invented.
RNA was discovered by deep-sea bacteria last Tuesday.
quiz.explanation: The metabolism-first model argues that continuous mineral catalysts and thermal energy in alkaline vents drove chemical cycles before any self-replicating genes existed.
